title: Hack Back Your Smartphone
coreMove: Redesign the phone so useful tools remain reachable and unplanned cues lose their default path to your attention.
sourcePressure: The chapter begins the personal-device stretch by treating the smartphone as a portable trigger source that can be reconfigured without abstinence fantasies.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: A weak run would demand a phone detox instead of changing the device's trigger design.

hook: Hack Back Your Smartphone as a labeled topic opener
counterintuition: phones are not the problem by itself
tryThisNow: set a timer and notice your distractions
examples: reused old-package object-anchor shell from earlier Indistractable run

exampleSpecs.domain: home-health nurse carrying a phone between patient visits
exampleSpecs.audience: nurse who needs maps and medication calls but not every alert
exampleSpecs.stakes: patient timing and privacy suffer when the whole device is treated as urgent
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she leaves map, secure call, and schedule visible while moving social icons into a search-only folder
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A privacy screen protector reflects a route list.

exampleSpecs.domain: wildlife photographer waiting in a blind
exampleSpecs.audience: photographer who needs camera controls but not feeds
exampleSpecs.stakes: one feed check can scare off the shot and break patience
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he pins the shutter remote and weather app while removing feeds from the home screen
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A shutter remote app sits beside a camouflage lens wrap.

exampleSpecs.domain: paramedic student using flashcards on commute breaks
exampleSpecs.audience: student whose study app sits beside video shortcuts
exampleSpecs.stakes: certification prep erodes in five-minute gaps
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: before, thumb opens video; after, flashcards sit alone on the dock during commute weeks
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A transit transfer slip lies under a flashcard widget.

exampleSpecs.domain: auction house specialist verifying lot numbers
exampleSpecs.audience: specialist who needs the camera and inventory app
exampleSpecs.stakes: wrong lots get photographed if alerts hijack the check
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she sets a lot-verification focus screen and silences collector-chat badges until noon
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A porcelain lot tag is framed by a phone camera grid.

exampleSpecs.domain: landscape crew lead coordinating weather and crews
exampleSpecs.audience: crew lead needing calls but not sports alerts
exampleSpecs.stakes: rain timing and crew placement depend on the right cues
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he keeps weather radar and crew calls, then deletes badge access for nonwork apps during shifts
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A muddy work glove points at a weather radar tile.

exampleSpecs.domain: museum visitor using audio guide with children
exampleSpecs.audience: parent who wants the guide but not message drift
exampleSpecs.stakes: the planned visit turns into scattered half-presence
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she opens audio guide mode, pockets the phone screen-down, and checks messages only at the courtyard bench
exampleSpecs.firstImage: An audio-guide lanyard rests beside a folded gallery map.
